note: Echo: فعلاً (13:42 Amal) = فعلين; بقيم (26:51 Amal) = بشيل; بعين/بعيم (26:52 Medi) = بشيل; كاسه (40:34/40:46 Amal) = كاسته. D22 (el- on أشيائي) needs audio: Amal heard el-, Medi denies it.

rulings.why: Cannot be verified - transcript hole: الليلة جو كتير كتير is missing its adjective, so the engine likely garbled the line (الليلة may be a mishearing); Amal's عن جد shows no confusion about the time.

row.why: He gave صلح (fix) a long-a form صلاحتو; Amal recast صلحته and he repeated it.

rulings.why: Same slip, both readers; the long-a form صلاحت is a wrong verb form she recast, matching the agreed A19 بزياد -> بزيد (tier 2).

row.medi_said: I think is كراجي electrician ... كراجي. This is a new word.
row.why: He said كهربجي as كراجي and Amal repeated it syllable by syllable.

rulings.why: She had just volunteered كهربجي at 09:10 (D16, tier 0); at 09:39 he tried to say it back as كراجي and she re-said كهـ، كهربجي - a wrong form of a word he had just been given, so tier 2.

row.why: Doubled verb ضل takes -eit for 'I' (ضليت); he said دلت/ضلت and Amal said 'what? ضليت'.

rulings.why: Same verb ضل; the slip is the I-past ending of a doubled verb (ضليت, not ضلت). That is a past-tense ending rule (B5), so it is grammar. د/ض is S4.

row.why: 'Because there is AC (at home)' is عشان في مكيف; يكون is not the plain present 'there is'. Amal let it pass. Reader's reading.

rulings.why: The real slip is r1's يكون for 'there is'. r2's piece (take Allah بيتي -> بـ/في) is dropped: Amal's 'بِ أو فِي بيتي؟' asks which word she heard, he said بي بيتي and she moved on, so nothing was wrong. r2's version of the يكون row is D18 (a duplicate).

row.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
row.why: Two of a noun takes the dual (فعلين), not noun + تنين; Amal's reply recasts it as فعلين (engine wrote فعلاً).

rulings.why: Her 13:42 'أههم بس فعلاً' reads as بس فعلين (engine wrote فعلاً): she recast his فعل تنين into the dual.
Not an error: مش قصدهم ('they didn't mean') is normal spoken Levantine, like مش قصدي; ما كان قصدهم is optional.

row.why: A singular verb for 'they'; Amal repeated 'They upset you' (stress on they) and he moved to the plural بيتايوك.
row.english: (it wasn't their intention) to upset you

rulings.why: Keep r1's piece: he gave 'they' a singular verb (بتدايك), Amal repeated 'They upset you' and he changed to the plural. r2's piece is the same as D9.

row.why: After قصدهم (intention + ending, like biddi) the second verb drops b-; Amal recast يدايقوكي and he repeated it with b-.
row.english: it wasn't their intention to upset you

rulings.why: After مش قصدهم the next verb has no b- (like after biddi). Amal recast يدايقوكي without b-, and he said بيتايوكي again. ق -> د/ت is S4.

row.why: For 'I remove' he said شول (root of شيل, wrong form); Amal gave the verb (engine wrote بقيم) and he echoed it. Low: the engine is garbled on both sides.

rulings.why: He did try the word: شول is شيل with the wrong vowel. Amal supplied the verb (engine wrote بقيم, it is بشيل) and he repeated it (engine بعين / بعيم). That is a wrong form he attempted, so tier 2, not tier 0.

row.why: Spoken 'you (pl)' past is -tu (انكسرتو); -tum is MSA. Amal let it pass.

rulings.why: In the conjugation list he gave the MSA ending -tum. Spoken Levantine uses -tu, and he himself said كسرتوا at 29:18. Amal let it pass.

Not an error: كاسته (kaast-o, 'his cup') is the correct feminine -t + ending (A3). Amal's كاسه is the engine spelling of the same word, and she then said 'كاسه انكسرت' = his cup broke, confirming it. Her only fix here is انكسر -> انكسرت (A23).
Duplicate of A2 / S4: at 03:03, one second after her عزمت, he is repeating her fix with a glottal onset (أعزمت). That is pronunciation of the ع, not a new wrong form.

row.why: 'On YouTube' is على/عَ اليوتيوب, not لـ; Amal let it pass. Reader's reading; the engine may have misheard عَ.
row.english: I watched a video on YouTube

rulings.why: 'A video on YouTube' takes على (عَ اليوتيوب); لـ is the wrong preposition. Amal let it pass. Low: the engine may have written عَ as لـ.
Not an error: رنّيت لـ (رنيتله, رنلي) is normal Levantine next to رنيت على.

row.amal_said: Or some people say كهربجي. It's easier.
row.why: Amal taught كهربجي (electrician), a new word, after his question; tier 0.

rulings.why: A didn't-know: he asked 'Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟' while looking for 'electrician', and Amal offered the new word كهربجي.

Duplicate of A6, same moment: her 'صلحني would be he fixed me ... صلح لي' was a step on the way to finding the verb he meant (ساعدني, which takes -ni correctly). The slip was the verb, and A6 already holds it.
Duplicate of D5 (same يكون -> في/فيه row; D5 holds it as B8 + C1).
Not an error: متأكتي is متأكدة said the Levantine way, mit2akkde/-i (ة after د is said -i), with ت/د as S4. The feminine ending is there.
Not an error / engine spacing: 'من هم' sounds the same as منهم (minhom); the engine split one word into two.
Likely engine: in the same drill he used b- on every other person (بيكسر, بتكسر, بنكسر), and 'humme bikasro' loses its b to the m before it in speech-to-text. Cannot be verified.

row.amal_said: أشياءي نوع الإل. (engine; = أشيائي بدون الـ)
row.wrong: الأشيائي (as Amal heard it; engine wrote أشيائي)
row.why: Amal reminded him that a noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; the engine shows no el- and Medi says 'I don't think I said ال' - needs audio.

rulings.why: Amal said out loud that he used el- on a possessive noun (engine 'نوع الإل' = without el-). The brief says to trust her echo over the engine, but he says he did not say ال, so confidence is low and it should go to an audio check.
Self-fix: in the 45:34 line he switched to هو بينكسر himself before Amal's 'هو' (which confirms it). He then gave هي بتنكسر, and at 45:25 her 'إنتو' only set the order of the drill.
Engine/stutter: 'بن-بنكسر' is bin-ninkiser (بننكسر) broken at the stutter, so the second n is there; Amal moved on.
